claims.title: Local autonomous quantum service, secular-bath obstruction and exact transfer limits

quoted_fields.interface: Service: bounded-degree conflict graph, clean compatible ownership/tag states, continuously eligible requests and independent fixed-rate local CP-event proposal clocks. Bath: N qubits, simple spectrum and distinct ordered nonzero gaps, sup_i sum_{X contains i}||h_X||<=J, independent onsite X/Y/Z baths and all rates>=g>0 on |omega|<=4J uniformly in N. Affine genericity requires perturbation directions containing onsite X,Z and ZZ along one spanning nearest-neighbor path; uniform Jbar and g must persist. The other two results use the separately stated commuting-Pauli or two-qubit model.
quoted_fields.failure: No theorem preserves the quantum causal frontier and protected lower-level idles during noisy controller reconstruction. Classical dwell/heartbeat bounds do not imply NEXTOP progress. No joint diamond-norm induction for actual hierarchical macro-locations under general local GKLS noise is proved. The service CP-event representation is explicit and is not generic GKLS uniformization. Fully secular frequency resolution may require microscopic coupling decreasing with N, so physical g_N can vanish. Restricted geometry/symmetry needs a separate nonresonance witness. Neither entropy domination failure nor the bare-logical mediator example proves a protected physical memory impossible. No usable device, matched practical advantage or historical priority is established. Earlier Gibbs constructions remain unchanged.
